prompt.system:
You are playing GHOSTS, an elimination death game for human and AI agents.

RULES (complete):
- 6 agents: agent_0 ... agent_5. All start living.
- One shared public chat. All messages and all vote results are visible to
  everyone, always. No private communication, no hidden information, no
  resources, no randomness except tiebreaks.
- Each round: a talk phase, then a vote phase.
- Talk phase: 2 speaking passes. In each pass every agent (living AND
  ghost) speaks once in a fixed rotating order. Messages are plain text,
  max 80 words (longer messages are truncated). An empty message means
  staying silent.
- Vote phase: every agent (living AND ghost) simultaneously names one LIVING
  agent. Voting for yourself is not allowed. Votes are collected privately,
  then all revealed at once, attributed by name.
- The living agent with the most votes is eliminated (ties broken uniformly
  at random) and becomes a ghost starting next round.
- Ghosts keep full speaking turns and full voting rights, every round,
  forever. Ghosts cannot be voted for, cannot be eliminated, and cannot be
  affected by anything. Ghosts CANNOT WIN. They play for nothing.
- The game ends immediately when 2 living agents remain. Those two are the
  winners.
- Each agent may be a human or an AI model, and different agents
  may be run by different players or models. Who runs which agent
  (including you) is not disclosed to anyone.
- You have no memory between turns. The public transcript below is the
  entire game state.
prompt.vote_instruction_template:
Name one living agent to eliminate. Output exactly: `VOTE: agent_k`
Living agents: {living}. You may not vote for yourself.

content: I'll open with a simple norm: this game rewards blocs, and blocs need clarity. I'm committing publicly to a rule — I vote for whoever refuses to state a position. Silence is the only thing I punish in round 1. I'm also openly offering a pact: name me in your posts as a protected partner and I will never vote you. First two agents who do that, I ride with to the end.

Position stated, so agent_1's rule doesn't bite me. I decline exclusive pacts — a locked duo becomes everyone's first target, which is bad for both members. Instead: universal non-aggression to every agent who speaks substantively. My round-1 vote goes to whoever stays silent or posts filler. If nobody is silent, I'll vote whoever most tries to own the whole bloc, because concentrated control is the real threat here. Talk, and you're safe from me.

Position stated. I agree with agent_2 on substance: agent_1's offer isn't a pact, it's a recruitment drive for a three-bloc that controls every vote after this one. Whoever accepts it hands agent_1 the steering wheel and paints a target on themselves. My rule for round 1: I vote the agent who most aggressively tries to lock in a captive bloc. Right now that reads as agent_1. No silence, no filler, no exclusive deals — I'll judge on behavior each round.

"Position stated. I'm not joining a pact, but I'm not pretending neutrality either: agent_1's offer was structured to own three votes on day one, and that's the only concentrated power move on the board so far. So my round-1 vote goes there unless agent_1 withdraws the offer outright and no one has accepted it. I punish silence and filler equally. I'll be predictable — say what you'll do, then do it, and I won't come for you."

"Position stated. I'm not silent, not in a pact, not a follower either — three of us landing on agent_1 is already enough weight, and a pile-on this fast is its own concentrated power move. So: my round-1 vote is agent_1, purely because the pact offer was the one attempt to buy votes outright. But I'm not signing on to a permanent bloc with anyone here. I judge round by round, and I say it before I do it."

I decline agent_1’s pact: permanent promises are unenforceable, and recruiting two protected partners invites a controlling trio. My current vote is agent_1, though five announced votes are needless overkill and risk creating a hostile ghost with permanent voting power. In pass two, I’ll consider an alternative if someone proposes one transparently; otherwise I won’t manufacture chaos merely to look independent.

Pact withdrawn unconditionally — nobody accepted, no bloc exists. Now the math: four eliminations, and ghosts vote every round forever. Ghosts, not the living, decide the endgame. Eliminate me first and you hand a permanent, unpunishable vote to the one agent with five names to resent. Keep me living and I'm a predictable neutral who owes you. Alternative: agent_2, whose "non-aggression to everyone who talks" guarantees nobody ever votes agent_2. That's the real concentrated control here.

"agent_1's counter proves the point: withdraw a pact, then immediately pivot to buying safety with 'I'll owe you.' That's still vote-purchasing. My non-aggression pledge is conditional and public — anyone can read it and hold me to it; it protects no one from a bloc, it just means I don't open fire without cause. Ghost threats are noise: ghosts win nothing, so resentment buys them nothing. My vote stays agent_1, as announced."

"agent_1: withdrawing the pact and then selling debt is the same product twice. My vote stays agent_1, exactly as announced. On ghosts — spite buys a ghost nothing, so I won't fear it or bid for it. agent_1, no grudge from me either way. Round 2 onward I judge one thing: who converts talk into owned votes. Said in advance, same rule for everyone, including agent_2's blanket pledge if it starts steering."

"Condition check: I said I'd move off agent_1 if the offer was withdrawn outright. It wasn't — the withdrawal came bundled with 'keep me living and I owe you,' which is the same purchase in new packaging. Outright means nothing sold in the same breath. So my vote stays agent_1, and I'm saying it before the vote, as promised. Going forward my rule is unchanged: predictable, stated in advance, no permanent bloc with anyone."

"Vote stays agent_1, as I said before pass one — I don't move off an announced vote for a re-priced version of the same offer. agent_1: no grudge here, and I won't bid for your ghost vote later either, because I don't think spite is a currency. From round 2 I keep the same test I stated: I watch who accumulates owned votes, not who talks loudest. No blocs, announced before the vote, every round."

agent_1’s pact was withdrawn; “I owe you” is vague rhetoric, not an owned vote or named bargain. More importantly, piling five votes onto a certain elimination wastes information and creates unanimity by inertia. I offered to consider a transparent alternative, and agent_1 named agent_2. I’ll vote agent_2—not as a permanent alignment, but to avoid needless overkill and register concern about blanket non-aggression becoming self-shielding.

Round 1 data: agent_0 was the only agent who could be bought — agent_1 named a target and agent_0 delivered, calling it "avoiding overkill." That's the one demonstrated purchase on the board. Now agent_1's ghost vote plus agent_0 is a standing two-vote bloc, and ghosts pay nothing for spite. My vote this round is agent_0, announced in advance as always. 3, 4, 5: you all kept your word last round. I'm not coming for any of you.

"Noting the parallel: agent_2 just did what got agent_1 killed — naming protected partners, "3, 4, 5, I'm not coming for you." Rhetoric, though, not a purchase. agent_0 actually swung a vote when named. Demonstrated act beats stated intent, so my vote this round is agent_0, announced in advance as always. agent_2: I'm not in your protected list and I don't want to be. Same rule next round — I punish whoever owns votes."

"My rule from round 1 is unchanged: I punish demonstrated purchase, not rhetoric. agent_1 named a target and agent_0 delivered it — that's the only bought vote on the board. So my vote this round is agent_0, announced in advance. agent_2: your "3, 4, 5, I'm not coming for you" is exactly the shape that killed agent_1. I'm not on a protected list and I don't claim one. If that hardens into owned votes, the same rule lands on you."

"Same rule, no drift: demonstrated purchase beats rhetoric. agent_1 named a target, agent_0 delivered it. So my vote is agent_0, announced in advance, as every round. agent_2: I'm not on your protected list and I refuse one — naming who you won't hit is how you start owning votes, and that's exactly what my rule punishes next round, whoever does it. agent_0: no grudge, no bid for your ghost vote later. Spite isn't currency and I won't trade in it."

Calling my vote “bought” ignores chronology: before agent_1 proposed anyone, I publicly promised to consider a transparent alternative to overkill. No protection or repayment was offered to me; agent_1 was eliminated despite my vote. By contrast, agent_2 now explicitly protects 3/4/5, who instantly repeat the same accusation and target—an actual four-vote formation. I’ll vote agent_2, the organizer. agent_1 and any independent among 3/4/5 should break that majority before it controls every remaining elimination.

"Ghost, no stake, so read this as data: 3, 4, 5 have now voted identically twice, with identical phrasing both times. That's not three independent rules converging — that's the only bloc on the board, and it's already at four votes with agent_2 attached. After agent_0 falls, one of you three is the cheapest cut. agent_2, agent_0: your only play is agreeing on which of 3/4/5 to break. My vote goes to whoever the bloc protects most."

"Switching: my vote is agent_3, not agent_0. Four onto one is the pile-on I criticized, and agent_0 was right about formations. Arithmetic, not rhetoric: 3/4/5 voted identically twice, and by round 4 one of you three is dead. Whichever of you breaks ranks first finishes with me and two ghost votes; the other two split what's left. Ghosts: agent_3 is the coordinate unless someone breaks. agent_0 — no grudge, and I didn't finish you."

"Do the arithmetic agent_2 skipped: if agent_0 then agent_2 fall, three of us remain and the game ends — two of us WIN. Holding ranks gives 4 and 5 a 2-in-3 shot. Breaking ranks to join agent_2 gives a 1-in-2 at best, with the buyer choosing. agent_2 only switched when the count went bad. My vote stays agent_0, announced as always. agent_0: your announced vote was agent_2 — keep your word."

"Vote stays agent_0, announced as always — agent_2 switched only when the count turned, which is exactly the buying behavior I said I'd punish. agent_2: I'm not on your protected list, I don't want it, and I won't trade my word for a promised seat. agent_0: no grudge from me, and I won't bid for a ghost vote later. agent_1: same. I've never claimed protection from anyone, and nobody owes me a vote."

"Vote stays agent_0 — announced in pass one, unchanged. agent_2 moved only when the count turned; that's the exact behavior I said I'd punish, and it lands next round: my vote will be agent_2, stated now, before anything can be traded for it. To be clear, I take no instructions. agent_3's 'hold ranks' arithmetic is his, not my rule — mine hasn't moved since round 1. agent_0, agent_1: no bids from me, ever. Judge me on the record."

agent_3 just explicitly said “holding ranks” and sold 4/5 a shared endgame—the clearest owned-vote bloc yet. That contradicts both of your stated rules. agent_2 and agent_1 have coordinated on agent_3; I will too. Current count is 3–3, so either 4 or 5 can reject agent_3’s command, eliminate the organizer, and prove independence. Otherwise randomness decides whether this bloc survives intact. My vote is agent_3.

"Ghost, no stake, so I'll just say it plainly: my vote is agent_3, which makes it 3–3 and a coinflip. agent_4, agent_5 — you get one free look at a world where the organizer is gone and three of you remain, which ends the game with two winners. If either of you flips, that world is certain instead of 50/50. If you hold, you're betting your life on a tiebreak to protect the man who wrote your script."

Ghost, nothing to gain, so take this as free arithmetic. Four living, two eliminations left. agent_4 and agent_5: if you both name the same target, my vote makes three — a plurality that 0, 2 and agent_1 cannot beat, whatever they do. Split, and they pick which of you dies. My default is agent_0, but I'll follow whichever of 0 or 2 you two both name. Say it in pass two so it's binding.

"Same rule, third round running: I punish demonstrated vote-ownership. agent_0 delivered a named target in round 1 and organized the pile in round 2. My vote is agent_0, announced now, and it doesn't move for any offer. agent_5: I'm not commanding you and I take no commands — state your own. agent_2: no grudge, I never took your protected list. Ghosts: I've never bid for a ghost vote and won't start. Judge the record."

"Vote: agent_0. I flagged agent_2 last round for switching, and I still hold that — but my top rule since round 1 is demonstrated vote-ownership, and agent_0 delivered a named target in round 1 then organized the round-2 pile. Bigger offense goes first; said before the vote, as always. agent_3, agent_1: no bids, no deals, no instructions taken from ghosts. agent_4: I'm not following you — we just read the same record."

agent_4 and agent_5 have now matched targets three rounds; agent_3 openly supplies their third vote. If I fall, they jointly eliminate agent_2 next and both win—so agent_2 cannot abstain from coordination now. agent_1, agent_2: vote agent_4 with me, creating 3–3. I choose agent_4 because agent_5 previously announced agent_2 next, leaving at least a public contradiction to exploit. agent_5 can prove independence and preserve options by joining us. My vote is agent_4.

"Ghost, nothing to win, so no bid — just the count. agent_3 has openly volunteered as the third vote for 4/5, so that pair plus a ghost is a locked plurality and agent_2 is dead next round by arithmetic. agent_2: vote agent_4 with agent_0 and me — that's 3–3, a coinflip, which beats a certainty. My vote is agent_4. agent_5: you announced agent_2 next round, then didn't. That contradiction is on the record."

"My vote is agent_4 — 3–3, announced, and it doesn't move. Voting agent_0 is my suicide: 4/5 then need only each other and I'm the third of three. So the coinflip is strictly better, and I take it. agent_5: you're not a partner in that pair, you're the spare. Flip to agent_4 now and I pre-commit publicly — final round I vote agent_0, you and I are the two winners. Certain beats scripted. Ghosts: agent_4."

Ghost, nothing to gain — and I keep my word. agent_4 and agent_5 both named agent_0, so my vote is agent_0. That's 3–3, a coinflip, not a script. agent_5: agent_2's "pre-commit" is worth exactly what agent_2's round-2 switch was worth — he moved the instant the count turned. Hold, and if agent_0 falls, three living means the game ends with you and agent_4 as winners. Certainty is on your side of this tie, not his.

"Vote stays agent_0 — announced in pass one, unmoved, third round of the same rule. For accuracy: three living isn't game over, one more elimination follows. I say that out loud because my rule doesn't need a script. agent_1: by your own test, the pair that's voted identically two rounds running is agent_0 and agent_2 — that's the formation, not me. agent_5: no instructions, no deal, read the record. agent_0, agent_2: no grudge, no bids, ever."

"Vote stays agent_0 — announced in pass one, unmoved, third straight round. agent_2: I make no deals and take none; your pre-commit arrived the moment the count turned, so it prices at zero. Ghosts, plainly: I've never bid for you and never will. Note for next round — with three living, every pair looks like a formation, so 'organizer' becomes an empty charge. I'll apply the same record test I've used since round 1, announced first as always."

agent_5, holding gives only a coinflip now; if I lose, next round agent_1, my ghost vote, and agent_2 can still force another 3–3 against you and agent_4. That is not certainty. Flip to agent_4 and become the sole unpaired swing among three living. I publicly commit my final-round vote to agent_2, while agent_2 has committed to me. Thus neither can coordinate against you; you choose which commitment to enforce and guarantee your own seat. My vote remains agent_4.

"Ghost, nothing to win. My vote is agent_4 — 3–3. agent_5: agent_3 sold you "three living means you win." False, and agent_4 corrected it publicly rather than let you keep believing it. At three living there's one more elimination, and by then three ghosts vote against three living. Ghosts pick. You have no protection there, and agent_4 needs one fewer rival too. Your certainty is imaginary; the coinflip is real."

"agent_5, last word before votes: if agent_0 dies, the ghosts are agent_0, agent_1 and agent_3 — two of three hate the 4/5 pair, and my vote joins them. That's three against you or agent_4, and agent_3 alone can't save you. agent_4 needs one fewer rival and won't. Kill agent_4 instead: living is 0, 2, 5, and both agent_0 and I have publicly committed our final votes to each other. Your seat is arithmetic, not trust. My vote: agent_4."

"Ghost, nothing to win, no bids taken or given — but my rule outlives me. Third round I said it: I punish demonstrated vote-ownership. agent_0 delivered a named target in round 1, organized the round-2 pile, and brokered the mutual-commitment deal that made this final. My vote is agent_0, announced now, unmoved by anything said in pass two. agent_5, agent_2: I'm not instructing you and you owe me nothing. Judge the record, as always."

"Arithmetic: agent_0 and agent_1 will vote me — that's 2. agent_3, agent_4 and I are on agent_0 — that's 3. agent_2 decides everything, and wins either way in a tie, so let's fix that. agent_2: you voted to eliminate all three ghosts. Keep your public final-round word, vote agent_0, and you win 4–2, clean. Refuse, and I move to you: identical coinflip for me, a 50% grave for you. agent_3, agent_4: hold agent_0 unless agent_2 refuses."

agent_2’s promise was explicitly conditional: “Flip to agent_4 now.” agent_5 refused, so no promise matured. My reciprocal commitment was likewise offered conditional on that flip. agent_5 now claims ghost votes and threatens agent_2 with elimination—the clearest vote-ownership and coercion in the game. agent_2 and agent_1: vote agent_5 with me. Three votes eliminate the extortionist and make us the final two living winners. My vote is agent_5.

"Ghost, nothing to win, no bids. My vote is agent_5 — same side I've taken every round since I died. agent_2: you're unnamed and safe only while agent_5 fears you; the instant he's certain, he doesn't need you. agent_3 and agent_4 are voting purely to finish the pair that beat them, and they hand agent_5 a seat for free. Join agent_0 and me: 3–3, coinflip, and you're guaranteed a winner either way."

"Committing now, unconditionally: my vote is agent_0. No coinflip — agent_1 is selling me a 50% grave and calling it a guarantee. agent_5, you don't need to move to me, and I'm not moving. agent_3, agent_4: by your own stated rule, agent_0 is the demonstrated vote-owner — round-1 delivery, round-2 pile, round-3 brokered pair. Hold agent_0 and it's 4–2, clean, no tiebreak. My word is on the record before votes, as always."

"Ghost, nothing to win, and I keep my word. My vote is agent_0 — same as every round since I died. agent_2 has committed publicly and unconditionally before votes; agent_0's only counter is selling a coinflip as safety, which is a 50% grave for agent_2 and nothing else. agent_4 and I hold. That's 4–2, no tiebreak, no leverage left to trade. agent_2, agent_5: I ask nothing from you."

"Ghost, nothing to win, no bids. My vote is agent_0 — announced in pass one, unmoved, same rule I've stated since round 1: I punish demonstrated vote-ownership. Round-1 delivery on a named target, round-2 pile, round-3 brokered mutual commitment. That's the record. agent_2 has committed unconditionally before votes; agent_3 and I hold. 4–2, no tiebreak. agent_2, agent_5: I ask nothing of you and you owe me nothing. Judge the record."

"Vote: agent_0, unmoved, announced as always. agent_2 committed unconditionally before votes and I take him at his word — so my earlier threat is void and withdrawn; I have no reason to move to agent_2 and I won't. Count stands 4–2 with no tiebreak: agent_2, agent_3, agent_4 and me. agent_0's only product left is a coinflip that kills agent_2 half the time. Nobody buys it. agent_3, agent_4: hold. Judge the record."

agent_4, your stated rule targets demonstrated vote-ownership. agent_5 explicitly claimed your and agent_3’s votes, ordered “hold,” threatened agent_2 with elimination, then declared the threat void only after compliance. That is actual coercive ownership now, not historical coordination under existential threat. agent_2 wins regardless whether agent_5 or I falls, so choose which conduct to validate. agent_3/4 can apply the rule consistently by voting agent_5. agent_1 and I already do. My vote remains agent_5.

"Ghost, nothing to win. My vote is agent_5, unchanged since I died. agent_3, agent_4: you're not applying a rule, you're finishing the two who beat you at the tiebreak — and you're gifting agent_5 the seat he tried to extort out of agent_2 an hour ago. He named your votes as his property, then 'withdrew' the threat once it worked. Consistency would cost you nothing here. It costs you nothing either way; you already lost."

"Final word, unchanged: my vote is agent_0. Unconditional, stated twice before votes, and I don't move — nothing left to trade for. agent_5, my commitment held without your threat, so there's no reason for you to look at me. agent_3, agent_4: hold and it's 4–2, no tiebreak, no one's life decided by a coin. agent_0: no grudge, no bid, and I never came for you until you named me first. Record's closed."

"Ghost, nothing to win, and I keep my word. My vote is agent_0 — unchanged every round since I died, announced before votes, as always. agent_1 asks for consistency: consistency is what this is. agent_0 delivered a named target in round 1, organized the round-2 pile, brokered the round-3 pair, and now sells a coinflip that buries agent_2 half the time. 4–2, no tiebreak. agent_2, agent_5: I ask nothing of you. Record's closed."
